﻿LANE 2 — INSTITUTIONAL KITCHENS
Start 14 Oct 2026 | India metro institutions first | Ownership: This document only
Mission: identify high-severity avoidable food waste in schools, colleges, hostels, offices, canteens, caterers, hospitals and elder-care facilities, disaggregating preparation loss, buffet leftovers and plate waste. Read Research Control Room per run.


HYPOTHESIS FOOD-03
Actual portions prepared fail to match attendance, demand, diet and timing; consequences = kilograms food discarded per meal, operating costs, wasted water/energy/land and possibly budgets available for food. Never count nutrition restriction or safe food handling as "waste" without context. Students and patients are protected populations; food suitability, allergies and sanitation constrain decisions.


COMPETITION
Winnow and Leanpath already provide AI vision logging, restaurant/kitchen waste categorization, dashboards and behavioral coaching; ordinary headcounts, procurement spreadsheets, Excel, ERP, menu planning and kitchen staff judgments are cheap substitutes. Do not claim image-recognition novel. Study small-facility adoption, economics and locally verified friction.


RESEARCH QUEUE
1. Find JAPAC ORIGINAL weighed food waste per meal for one institution type, with numerator, denominator, pre/post measurement.
2. Identify original causes (menu preference, class attendance, buffet uncertainty, hospital diet, serving-size design) and which are actually actionable.
3. Check adoption and product capability for Winnow/Leanpath, and local low-cost providers, in 2026; analyze affordability only with sourced quotes or documented budgets.
4. Seek legally/publicly available meal count + waste datasets, and external validity of any intervention studies.
5. Compare Gemini explanation/workflow automation and human-safe orchestration vs simple forecast / deterministic count. Distinguish pre-service leftovers from served food, donation eligibility.
6. Kill if straightforward count-based forecasting or existing product adequate, or no authentic data/authority to change prep.


CURRENT VERDICT: ADVANCE TO DATA ACCESS AUDIT; residual unmet need UNKNOWN; experiment NOT RUN.
SOURCE STARTERS
https://www.winnowsolutions.com/
https://www.leanpath.com/
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S095965262403645X
https://wedocs.unep.org/handle/20.500.11822/45230
APPEND DATED RUN ENTRIES BELOW.


Research update: original institutional kitchen studies located on 14 October 2026.


FOOD-03A | Campus mess attendance and preparation | 14 Oct 2026
Provisional verdict: NARROW. Investigate a specific gap in knowing how many students will actually eat a particular meal; do not presume GenAI is necessary.


India original physical baseline: Davison et al. (published 3 May 2022) measured approximately 45 kg of daily food waste at a Maharashtra university canteen serving 375 students (120 g per catered student-day) during Jan–Feb 2020. Following reopening, about 9 kg/day was measured among 150 students (60 g/student-day) in Dec 2020–Jan 2021. The apparent 50% per-person decline cannot be assigned to one intervention because occupancy, dining format, menus, and outside eating options changed during COVID. These are daily figures, not per meal, and do not separate preparation, service, and plate waste. Underlying records are not publicly shared. Source: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14095486


Independent India qualitative study: Rajalakshmi and Harshavardhini (April 2025), interviews with 50 hostel students, identified outside ordering without notice (20% of respondents), overpreparation (45%) and poor taste (60%) among perceived causes. These percentages are not weighed waste incidence. Source: https://doi.org/10.4103/jme.jme_118_24


Japan independently weighed evidence: Nakagiri et al. (PLOS ONE, 26 Feb 2024) measured returned side-dish containers at 20 elementary/junior-high schools supplied by one communal kitchen across 116 days. The median leftover rate was 20.1% for 250 selected high-leftover side dishes (range 0–96.9%), not the average for all meals or all food. Class size, nutrition-teacher assignment and elapsed time since cooking were associated with leftovers; adjusted R-squared 0.236. Supporting XLSX tables are published and could support reproducible analysis, though transferability to India is unknown. Source: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0298691


Additional India evidence: Reshmi and Srikanth (24 June 2025) observed/interviewed 11 Bengaluru educational cafeterias, identifying weak first-in-first-out inventory, expiration/freshness issues, forecasting and cold storage. No verified edible kilograms per meal or controlled intervention. These inventory failures differ from attendance-driven waste. Source: https://doi.org/10.36713/epra22674


Critical competitive correction: Winnow Foresight currently advertises standalone, mobile-only item-level production forecasts based on occupancy and waste history, without additional hardware. Leanpath offers tablet-only Tracker Lite, mobile Snap AI, and plate-waste analysis. Therefore no-hardware forecasting and AI plate logging are not unique. Published Indian small-site adoption, pricing and independent performance remain unknown. Sources: https://www.winnowsolutions.com/winnow-foresight and https://www.leanpath.com/products/


Root cause and alternatives: The Indian canteen study describes unpredictable mess attendance, students choosing outside meals, regional menu preferences and self-service overfilling. During COVID, better student attendance information, table service, fewer outside choices and smaller servings all changed together. Cheap alternatives are opt-out deadlines, basic headcount plus day-of-week forecasting, historical portions, smaller initial servings with seconds, manual waste weighing, and menu feedback. No evidence yet shows these fail. Food quality and sufficient meals must be maintained.


AI-specific hypothesis only: If dining intentions arrive as messy, inconsistent notes, a grounded Gemini workflow might classify changes and request confirmation, while deterministic code computes quantities. But standard forms, simple rules and conventional forecasting may be more reliable and cheaper. No model evaluation, consented campus integration, procurement integration or product deployment has been performed.


Falsification test (NOT RUN): Obtain permission for 14–28 days of actual diners by meal, timestamped advance dining intentions, dish-level planned versus cooked quantities, and separately weighed edible unserved food, plate waste and inedible preparation scraps. Compare current chef planning, simple headcount/opt-out rules, conventional forecasting, and an optional Gemini-assisted interpretation workflow on held-out days. Outcomes: kilograms of avoidable edible waste per actual meal served, forecasting error, food sufficiency, meal satisfaction, operator time and ingredient cost. Use food-specific environmental factors only with a defensible avoided-production/disposal counterfactual. Stop if rules work as well, existing competitors already solve the workflow, or authentic data is inaccessible.


Research status: underlying severity evidenced at selected sites; prevalence, edible fraction, unmet need after alternatives, willingness to pay and technical advantage UNKNOWN. Problem Value Score /100 withheld. Hackathon rubric technical 40%, impact 25%, innovation 25%, UX 10% remains separate. Strongest rejection: current attendance rules or Winnow/Leanpath eliminate the incremental AI value. Do not claim avoided emissions, hunger reduction or savings. NEXT: data-access audit of one India campus operator and public Japanese supplementary XLSX reproduction.




RESEARCH UPDATE — 14 OCT 2026, 10:31 IST — FOOD-03B: HOSPITAL WARD↔KITCHEN MEAL-STATUS HANDOFF
Research stage: independently corroborated severity + root-cause evidence → incumbent red-team → data-access falsification. Distinct from previous campus-mess FOOD-03A. VERDICT: NARROW TO HOSPITAL MEAL-STATUS EXCEPTIONS; DO NOT ASSUME GENAI VALUE.


PRECISE WORKFLOW AND USERS
A hospital dietitian prescribes the permitted diet; ward nurse and bed-management team record admissions, transfers, discharge, nil-by-mouth/procedure status and meal requests; kitchen manager commits production quantities before a cutoff; staff plate and deliver trays; patient may eat, defer or decline. Meal demand becomes inaccurate when clinically authorized status changes do not reach the kitchen before irreversible preparation. This is a candidate exception-handling problem, not a proposal to override clinical diets or automatically suppress nutrition.


NEW ORIGINAL JAPAC QUANTIFICATION — AUSTRALIA
E-L2-2026-01: Ni et al., Waste Management, published 15 Jan 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.wasman.2025.115242. Audit performed Sep–Oct 2023 at ONE 355-bed acute-care hospital in Adelaide; kitchen also supplied eight external sites (393 beds), so its total kitchen denominator is not identical to the three wards used for plate observations. Direct weighing + photographic/visual estimates across a full menu cycle: seven breakfasts, 21 lunches, 21 dinners; 2,616 plated meals from selected wards, 2,214 plates returned and audited (402, or 15%, missing). Mean kitchen food waste = 134.1 kg/day or 170.4 g per meal PRODUCED. Breakdown: unserved 117.5 kg/day = 149.3 g/meal (87.6% of kitchen food waste), preparation 16.3 kg/day = 20.7 g/meal, spoilage 0.3 kg/day = 0.4 g/meal. Edible preparation fraction = 14.7 kg/day = 18.7 g/meal; inedible = 1.5 kg/day = 2.0 g/meal. Plate waste on the three observed wards averaged 0.7 kg per patient-DAY (NOT per meal), or 40.7% of food served; special diets 49.4% vs regular diets 36.4% in diet-identified subset, with pureed diets especially high. Article explicitly notes meals prepared for patients scheduled for surgery or discharge as one contributor to unserved food, but does NOT quantify its attributable fraction. Other limitations: single site; liquid waste excluded; 15% of plate trays not returned; hospital supplied offsite locations; prep work outsourced upstream in part; original individual-level dataset NOT shareable because authors lacked permission. No controlled AI intervention or avoidable share proven. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wasman.2025.115242


INDEPENDENT JAPAC TRIANGULATION — MALAYSIA
E-L2-2025-02: Manimaran et al., BMC Health Services Research, published 10 Feb 2025, DOI 10.1186/s12913-025-12365-w. Qualitative original field research: 15 experienced participants in three focus groups (catering managers/officers, dietitians, nurses, academics from Malaysian public/private care settings). They specifically report outdated manual/online meal orders because admission, discharge, transfer and diet-status updates are not timely; ward-kitchen communication failures; procedure-related missed meals; automatic default meal ordering; patient appetite, choice and staff workload. These are reported mechanisms from purposively sampled staff, NOT measured rates, not a randomized intervention and not evidence that all hospitals have this problem. Direct: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12913-025-12365-w
E-L2-2024-03: Kassim et al., published 27 Nov 2024 in IJHHS supplementary issue, DOI 10.31344/ijhhs.v8i40.749: 239 inpatient plate-waste observations at a Malaysian university hospital, estimated using Comstock six-point VISUAL scale (NOT directly weighed). Mean 48.1% food served estimated discarded; therapeutic diets common in sample. This corroborates possible patient intake/waste severity, NOT meal-order handoff causality. Direct: https://doi.org/10.31344/ijhhs.v8i40.749
E-L2-2025-04: Idid, Universiti Sains Malaysia thesis, June 2025; 99 therapeutic-diet adult inpatients April–early June 2025, plate waste estimated via visual Comstock + digital photos, mean 40.77% (SD 26.7%). Overall foodservice satisfaction and plate-waste percentage were not significantly correlated (r≈0.032, p=0.751). Counterevidence against a simplistic “improve satisfaction and waste falls” assumption. Thesis not direct weighing, small single-center sample. https://erepo.usm.my/handle/123456789/23552


ADDITIONAL DIRECTLY WEIGHED AUSTRALIAN INDEPENDENT SITE AUDIT
E-L2-2023-05: Collins and Porter, Nutrition & Dietetics, 2023, DOI 10.1111/1747-0080.12796. Three Victoria hospitals audited over 14 weekdays (data collected 2018); aggregate mean 327.3 kg/day ORGANIC food waste = 227.7 kg/day plate + 99.6 kg/day trayline (includes expired). Separate packaging 174.8 kg/day; combined food+packaging 502.1 kg/day. Median 171 spare trays/day; 224 unused tray items/day cost AU$214.10/day in that specific system. These are aggregate daily site figures, NOT per-meal or per-patient; number of meals served not published as reliable denominator, and kitchen prep at central offsite facility excluded. At one site food went to wastewater disposal, so do NOT claim all food went to landfill. Original article directly notes the lack of meal-normalized data. Source: https://doi.org/10.1111/1747-0080.12796


COMPETITOR AND CHEAP-SUBSTITUTE RED TEAM — NEW MATERIAL FINDING
Indian product MedMeals by MealPe explicitly advertises dietitian-approved menus, meal hold/discharge, HIMS sync, ward/bed transfer, bedside ordering, kitchen tickets, meal status and billing; its HIMS integration page says future meals stop on discharge. This is a vendor-advertised capability, NOT independently verified deployment, outcomes or a published API. It directly challenges any claim that linking patient admission/discharge to meal preparation is novel. Sources: https://medmeals.mealpe.app/ and https://medmeals.mealpe.app/features/hims-integration/
Dietech advertises hospital EMR HL7/FHIR ADT + diet-order integration, room service and bedside tray verification; evidence of a mature generic integration pattern, not measured impact. Source: https://www.dietechsoftware.com/solutions/hospitals
Previously documented Winnow Foresight (mobile-only production forecast) and Leanpath (plate/waste logging) remain relevant for measurement and forecasts but are not replacements for clinical diet order controls.
Cheaper controls: existing HIMS/EMR ADT event feed + rules for meal cutoff, NPO/fasting flags from authorized clinical orders, ward-to-kitchen confirmation, census-based production buffers, late change exceptions, patient opt-in where clinically appropriate, audit trail and manual scale. None requires GenAI to perform core logic. Need evidence these controls fail in an accessible target institution before advancing.


POTENTIAL AI ROLE — HYPOTHESIS, NOT DEMONSTRATED
A constrained, grounded Gemini/agent workflow might reconcile unstructured ward messages, late procedure notices, dietitian-approved menu constraints and kitchen exceptions, classify ambiguous statuses, request human confirmation and create traceable alerts to a deterministic scheduling system. It must NEVER infer or alter diet orders, NPO status, allergies or medical restrictions from generated text. Authenticated EHR/HIMS event feeds and rules take precedence; model must not handle identifiable clinical records without approvals, and no automated cancellation of clinically required meals. General LLM plus rules and established HIMS integration are strong comparators; agent complexity may add latency and safety risk. The presence of messy text does not establish incremental AI benefit.


MEASUREMENT / IMPACT BOUNDARIES
Primary numerator: grams/kg of avoidable EDIBLE unserved food discarded before any patient handling, by dish and meal service. Denominator: meals actually produced, and optionally kg per patient-meal ordered/served. Track plate waste separately (g/plate and % of served), and prep edible vs inedible separately. Measure meal-order change-to-kitchen latency, duplicate trays, late changes, number of clinically required meals fulfilled on time, patient nutrient adequacy, kitchen labor and ingredient cost. Do not multiply Australia's 149.3 g/meal by Indian hospital census and claim a prediction. Do not infer all unserved food is avoidable; safety buffers and diet requirements matter. Any CO2e/water estimate needs food-specific composition, local supply chain and avoided-production/disposal counterfactual; AI inference and extra computing footprint must be deducted where material. Social benefit = protecting patient meal access/nutrition and hospital budgets, NOT a claim of donations or reduced malnutrition.


DATA ACCESS / LICENSING
Ni et al. explicitly: authors do not have permission to share individual dataset. Published aggregate figures are available under open-access journal license; original hospital event and meal records NOT available to this project. Malaysian qualitative quotes and public abstract available, but no time-stamped linked hospital meal records. India hospital HIMS feeds and procurement data: NOT ACCESSED, no partner approval, no authenticated vendor integration. MedMeals prices, small-site deployments and independent performance: UNKNOWN. Do not represent a demo with synthetic data as empirical impact.


ONE DECISIVE FALSIFICATION TEST — NOT RUN
With authorized hospital and clinical oversight, retrospectively obtain 14–28 days of pseudonymized time-stamped (a) meal orders and actual plating cutoff, (b) clinically approved diet/order status, (c) admission/discharge/transfer/procedure event timestamps, (d) kitchen production and weighed edible unserved/plate waste, (e) meals delivered and missed or delayed. Establish exact number and kg of trays prepared AFTER an authoritative status change that a basic ADT/HIMS rule could have prevented. On held-out periods compare: A current process, B deterministic event-driven ADT sync + cutoff/confirmation rules, C existing meal-management vendor or feature, D optional Gemini interpreting only residual unstructured approved notes. Success requires an independently observed, recurring residual kg of avoidable edible waste and no clinically missed nutrition; Gemini must demonstrably improve precision/recall, human minutes or resolution time beyond B/C, without safety errors. REJECT GenAI angle if B/C eliminate most avoidable waste, or if clinical data access impossible. A public synthetic scenario can demonstrate technical handling but cannot pass the impact gate.


VERDICT AND STAGE
NARROW / CONDITIONAL ADVANCE TO DATA ACCESS AUDIT. The underlying waste severity is supported by original 2026 Australian direct weighing and multiple independent Malaysian studies. Specific late-order/ward communication mechanism is documented qualitatively. BUT causal share, target India/JAPAC prevalence, buyer budget, verified product gap, authorized dataset and incremental GenAI advantage are UNKNOWN. Strongest rejection: EMR/HIMS integration and simple status-change rules already solve the key handoff; clinical safety and access are high barriers. Next run should move to a different institutional subsegment (e.g., office canteen buffet or school meal serving) or investigate a real hospital implementation outcome rather than restating these findings. Problem Value /100 WITHHELD; hackathon 40/25/25/10 cannot be scored without a tested solution. No user interviews, model evaluations, experiments, savings, deployments or partner approvals performed.


14 October 2026: Workplace canteen research update pending source review.


FOOD-03C: A published study of four Beijing workplace buffet canteens weighed 656 returned plates. Average edible lunch leftovers were 78.8 grams per diner. This is plate waste, not kitchen overproduction. Data access and transfer to India remain unverified.


Study details: Zhang et al., Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems, published 3 December 2024, DOI 10.3389/fsufs.2024.1455756. Four Beijing buffet sites, 656 valid samples from August-September 2021. Each site was sampled for only two weekdays. Solid edible leftovers were weighed; liquids and unserved stock were excluded.
Source URL: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/sustainable-food-systems/articles/10.3389/fsufs.2024.1455756/full


E-L2C-01, environmental impact: The Beijing study modeled 423.67 litres of water and 1.566 kg CO2-equivalent embodied in the food discarded per diner-day. These are lifecycle burdens, not verified savings. Livestock foods represented about 29.9% of discarded weight but 85.7% of modeled water footprint and 63.2% of carbon footprint. This is not an India impact factor. Higher menu diversity and outsourced management correlated with higher waste, without proving causality. Individual research records were offered by authors on request but were not obtained.


E-L2C-02, independent JAPAC context: A China Agricultural University report dated 13 December 2024 covered four Beijing university canteens and reported 74.83 grams of edible leftovers per student-meal, 44% vegetables and 39% staples. This is a different student population, not an independent workplace replication. Its intervention summary combines multiple methods and does not establish AI effectiveness. Source: https://agfep.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/12/13/art_39035_1048826.html


E-L2C-03, non-JAPAC counterevidence: Daker and colleagues, Scientific Reports, 24 December 2025, measured 13,150 anonymous corporate-cafe plate scans in Europe and the US. In controlled comparisons, static social-norm and portion-choice signs prevented an estimated 11.8 grams per lunch diner, about 31% relative to a 38.2-gram baseline. Some treatment sites still increased but less than controls. The top 10% of plates accounted for 31-62% of measured waste; this does not establish the same people waste repeatedly. No GenAI was needed. DOI: 10.1038/s41598-025-28175-3.


E-L2C-04, India incumbent correction: Compass Group India says digital food-waste tracking covered over 90% of its sites in 2025, versus over 75% in 2024. September 2026 reporting of its 2025 sustainability report attributes a decline in waste from 8% to 3% at selected sites to SmartQ AI production planning, alongside 2-3% monthly cost savings. These are company-reported figures; the denominator, independent controls and causal attribution were not verified. SmartQ already sells POS, preordering, menu analytics, kitchen planning and waste optimization. It even describes menu co-occurrence-aware rice forecasts. A generic menu-aware AI forecast is therefore not novel.


Competitor sources: https://compass-group.co.in/sustainability/ ; https://www.thesmartq.com/ ; https://www.thesmartq.com/blogs/brsr-and-the-boardroom-what-corporate-cafeteria-management-has-to-do-with-your-esg-score ; https://www.fnbnews.com/Top-News/compass-group-india-releases-sustainability-report-2025-87777 . Other incumbents already logged: Winnow Foresight, Leanpath, Orbisk. Orbisk: https://orbisk.com/ . Product claims establish advertised capabilities, not independently verified effectiveness, site pricing or integration rights.


Unmet-need hypothesis only: A small Indian workplace cafeteria may struggle with late event/attendance updates and changed dish availability after production is committed. A grounded Gemini agent might reconcile authorized unstructured notes, but simple headcounts, POS, historical forecasting, smaller batches, half portions and static signs are cheaper alternatives. No evidence yet shows these late changes are a major cause of observed plate waste. The Beijing study measured plate leftovers, not buffet overproduction. Model-specific advantage, small-site affordability and access to Indian records are UNKNOWN.


Falsification test: With site consent, collect 14-28 days of meal counts, planned and prepared quantities by dish, event updates and physical weights separated into edible plate waste, unserved buffet food, and preparation scraps. Compare existing chef practice with simple headcount forecasts, smaller portions, static signs and established vendor tools. Only then test whether an AI workflow handles a remaining documented decision better.


Evaluation and verdict: Measure grams of avoidable edible waste per meal, meal availability, satisfaction, operator time, costs and food-specific environmental factors. No study, AI test or site integration has been run. NARROW: original physical evidence establishes the problem at selected sites, but unmet need beyond SmartQ/Winnow/Leanpath/Orbisk and low-cost controls remains unknown. Reject an AI product if basic forecasting and signage solve the issue or if real operational data is inaccessible. Problem Value /100 withheld; hackathon 40/25/25/10 separate and unscored. Next distinct inquiry: affordable small Indian canteen adoption and real operator access.


Source links for E-L2C-03: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-28175-3 . Source review completed for FOOD-03C; the earlier placeholder should be read as superseded by the detailed evidence entries. The reported figures above are source observations or company claims, never demonstrated benefits of our proposed product.




14 OCT 2026 — FOOD-03D — SCHOOL LUNCH WASTE AND NUTRITION (VIET NAM / INDONESIA)
Verdict: ADVANCE problem evidence to validation; NARROW generic AI menu and waste scanning. Distinct from previous campus, hospital and office research.
Vietnam primary study (Nguyen et al., Appetite, 1 Apr 2023, DOI 10.1016/j.appet.2023.106485): 1,720 individually weighed student-lunch plate observations in 12 peri-urban schools, two sampling days per school. Mean edible plate waste 85 g/student-lunch (SD 72), 23% served. Vegetable dishes 49% discarded, rice 15%, protein dishes 27%. Mean vegetable portion offered only 49.9 g; study notes this was around one quarter of daily vegetable recommendation. Larger portions correlated with more food discarded AND more food eaten. Soup waste was not measured; rice mixed with soup may distort weights; no kitchen pre-service waste captured. Cross-sectional, not causal; published 15.3 kg per school-year is extrapolated. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.appet.2023.106485
Indonesia independent corroboration: Zuhra et al., J Health Nutr Res, 1 Apr 2026, DOI 10.56303/jhnresearch.v5i1.924. East Aceh: 106 purposively sampled students in three schools, weighed over 10-day menu cycle. Mean 24.3% of served food discarded; middle school 29.8%, high school 16.5%. Staple foods, vegetables, plant-based sides most wasted. Authors modeled nutrient losses equivalent to 12 child lunches per year; not an actual year of missing meals. Raw individual data not downloadable on publisher page. Source: https://www.journalmpci.com/index.php/jhnr/article/view/924
Indonesia further corroboration: Muthmainnah et al., Jurnal Gizi Klinik Indonesia, July 2025, DOI 10.22146/ijcn.116242. Yogyakarta, 52 elementary students, seven days of measured plate waste. Reported aggregate mean daily 2,484.1 +/- 745.1 g (NOT per-student); carbohydrate/side-dish preferences correlated with leftovers; knowledge score did not (p=.080). Small observational sample. Source: https://journal.ugm.ac.id/jgki/article/view/116242
Root cause hypothesis: nutrition planner, cooks and teachers receive different information on portion, texture, meal temperature, menu acceptability and actual intake. Reducing waste by simply shrinking nutritious portions could worsen child nutrition. Need measure consumed nutrients AND avoidable discarded grams, not plate waste alone.
Current competition: Indonesia BGN already launched school meal-quality feedback app Reviu Menu MBG in May 2026, capturing food quality and delivery observations. https://www.bgn.go.id/news/berita/bgn-perkuat-pencegahan-kejadian-menonjol-mbg-luncurkan-aplikasi-pemantauan-kualitas-makanan-di-sekolah . India cloudeUNI advertises AI menu planning, attendance-aware waste forecasts, cost and sentiment optimization; savings are unverified vendor claims. https://www.cloudeuni.com/module-mess.aspx . Smart Bin AI already advertises school plate scanning and dish-level analytics; claimed reductions not independently verified. https://smartbinai.com/ . Winnow/Leanpath/Orbisk also cover overlapping foodservice tasks. Low-cost substitutes: sampled scale weighing, chef and teacher feedback, better cooking/temperature, age-appropriate portions with seconds, simple attendance and menu rules.
Potential Gemini role only if unstructured multilingual feedback is a remaining bottleneck: grounded synthesis of authorized menu, recipe and staff observations, structured exceptions and human-reviewed recommendations under fixed nutrition requirements. Compare against paper/forms, rules, forecasting/ERP and ordinary Gemini; no AI model evaluation performed.
Falsification (NOT RUN): obtain permissioned 14–28 days at one school with dish-level served grams, weighed plate returns, separate unserved/preparation waste, menu and temperature logs, attendance, and dietitian-defined nutrient standards; no identifiable student records. Compare basic menu/portion/timing adjustments before adding AI. Primary outcomes: grams avoidable edible plate waste per meal and nutrients actually consumed, without reducing adequate meal access. Reject AI angle if simpler interventions or existing products suffice, or if authentic data inaccessible. No local India baseline, raw research dataset, independent vendor effectiveness, user budget or integration permission confirmed.
Severity supported at selected sites; addressable fraction and incremental GenAI benefit UNKNOWN. Problem Value /100 withheld; hackathon 40/25/25/10 unscored. Next: India PM POSHAN data and public school-meal records audit.


14 OCT 2026 | FOOD-03E | INDIA SCHOOL-MEAL MONITORING AND CONSUMPTION GAP
Verdict: NARROW. New original India evidence clarifies nutritional stakes and reveals that attendance-based cooking is already an established workflow. No Indian school plate-waste weights found in this run.
ASSAM government PM POSHAN 2024-25: School heads inform cooks of daily attendance BEFORE cooking, and cooks prepare to attendance-based norms; daily stock registers exist. Reported 44,106 schools and 3,145,412 average children served (2024-25). Nutritional entitlements: primary 450 kcal/12g protein; upper primary 700 kcal/20g protein. Material allowance Rs 6.78 and Rs 10.17 per child-day from May 2025, not full meal cost or technology budget. https://dee.assam.gov.in/portlets/pm-poshan
KARNATAKA official 2024-25 Programme Approval Board: Automated Monitoring System received reports from 42,146 of 53,284 schools (about 79%, rounded 80% in report). 62 NGO-run central kitchens covered 5,329 schools and 743,625 students. AMS records meals served, not food actually consumed or wasted. These administrative numbers do not prove overproduction. https://pmposhan.education.gov.in/Files/PAB/PAB-2024-25/Minutes-PAB-2024-25/Karnataka-PAB%20Minutes.pdf
BENGALURU original cross-sectional study, published 29 July 2023: 345 students in five government schools; about 1 in 3.6 had protein intake deficiency and 1 in 7.5 had both protein and calorie deficiency. No weighed plate waste or AI outcome. https://www.ijcmph.com/index.php/ijcmph/article/view/11343
GUNTUR original 2024 sample published 31 March 2026: 200 PM POSHAN upper-primary beneficiaries, 40% classified undernourished by BMI, 10% overweight/obese. Not comparable to Bengaluru's intake measure; no direct waste measurement. https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/TJRA/article/view/178842
PUNE private secondary canteens, data collected Feb-Apr 2020, published 17 December 2025: 32 schools and 64 food handlers; 42.2% knew FSSAI school-food guidelines, 54.7% identified nutritious foods; no food-waste weights. Sample stopped early due to pandemic. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-025-25666-w
COMPETITION: Government attendance-before-cooking rules and AMS already exist. Winnow, Leanpath, SmartQ, manual scales, spreadsheet headcounts, nutrition standards and staff feedback cover much of the generic AI forecasting/waste tracking proposition. FSSAI 2020 school-food regulations constrain nutrition and hygiene. https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Gazette_Notification_Safe_Food_Children_07_09_2020.pdf
GAP HYPOTHESIS: Daily meals SERVED are not equal to nutrients CONSUMED or edible waste prevented. Is an unstructured menu/acceptability exception unresolved after cheap teacher feedback and simple rules? Gemini could synthesize authorized multilingual feedback, but its incremental value is UNTESTED. Reject if conventional feedback and approved menus suffice.
DECISIVE TEST NOT RUN: With one school/central-kitchen partner, obtain 14-28 days of aggregate attendance, planned/actual dish weights, separate unserved edible, plate edible and inedible scraps, plus approved nutrition standards and anonymous menu feedback. Compare current practice, attendance/feedback rules, deployed vendor, and optional grounded Gemini. Outcomes: edible grams wasted per meal, adequate nutrition, operator time and actual costs. Winnow and Leanpath already offer kitchen waste analytics and AI guidance.


https://www.winnowsolutions.com/


https://www.leanpath.com/solutions/


Indian MedMeals already advertises diet orders, bedside ordering and hospital sync.


https://medmeals.mealpe.app/


Small Indian hospital buyer, pricing and willingness to pay: UNKNOWN.


Compare QR headcounts and staged cooking first.


Residual hypothesis: late ward changes may not reach the chef before dinner batches.


Agent role only if proven: source-linked exception queue with chef approval.


Rules for structured updates; ML for demand forecasts.


Diet changes and meal cancellations require clinician approval.


Test NOT RUN: 28-day matched-menu kitchen audit.


Weigh edible prep, untouched surplus, serving-line and plate waste separately.


Record actual meals, order changes, procurement and cooking cutoff times.


Compare manual workflow, QR plus rules, incumbent software, then grounded AI.


Outcomes: edible kg per meal, nutrition, quality and labor.


Water and emissions benefits: UNKNOWN without ingredient-specific factors.


Reject if cheap rules suffice or events arrive after cooking.


No AI test or saving measured. Problem Value /100 WITHHELD.


Technical 40/25/25/10 rubric UNSCORED. NARROW only.


Strongest rejection: incumbents already address most waste.


14 Oct 2026 22:35 IST | FOOD-03N | Office buffet lunch plate waste | Provisional DEFER generic GenAI; NARROW to low-cost portion and menu validation.
Original JAPAC: Zhang et al., published 3 Dec 2024, physically weighed 656 plates at four Beijing workplace buffet canteens over two days each in Aug-Sep 2021. Mean edible solid lunch plate waste was 78.8 g per observed diner-meal (0.0788 kg); 327 lunch plates. Pre-service, unserved kitchen and buffet-line edible kg per actual meal were NOT measured. The reported 158.4 g daily per capita is derived from meal averages, not repeat measurements of the same person. Raw records are promised by authors but not downloaded; article CC BY. https://doi.org/10.3389/fsufs.2024.1455756
Independent China university canteen study: Qian et al., 26 Jan 2022, weighed leftovers from 9,192 sampled students across 29 universities: 61.03 g plate waste per student-meal, not office waste. https://doi.org/10.3390/su14031411


FOOD-03N competition and cheaper baselines: Winnow Foresight launched 29 Sep 2026, mobile standalone item-level forecasts using occupancy and waste history, marketed to lighter hotel kitchens; no independent office result or Indian small-site price. https://www.winnowsolutions.com/winnow-foresight . Leanpath provides kitchen measurement, AI guidance and Snap AI at off-site corporate lunches: https://www.leanpath.com/ ; https://info.leanpath.com/snap-ai . Indian ZenEats advertises employee preorders, forecasting and waste analytics; percentage-saving claim unverified: https://www.zeneats.co.in/ . Mealy advertises QR preorders and pickup slots, BASIC ₹599/month for small canteens, but real fit/fees/adoption unverified: https://www.mealy.in/ . MessMitra advertises QR attendance, POS and inventory: https://messmitra.com/ . Baselines: opt-in headcounts, POS counts, calibrated manual weighing, recipe sheets, smaller plates/half portions, batch replenishment and weekday moving-average forecasts. Truly affordable office-kitchen segment and buyer willingness = UNKNOWN.


FOOD-03N mechanism and impact: Beijing workplace study excluded inedible food and liquids and did NOT weigh preparation, untouched kitchen surplus or exposed buffet-line discard. Its cross-canteen association between lower menu diversity and less plate waste is NOT causal. The reported 423.67 L water and 1.56622 kg CO2e per nominal person-day are modelled resource burdens, NOT avoidable savings or Indian transfer factors; original site-specific edible kg, purchasing costs, emissions and water avoided remain UNKNOWN. Root cause could be oversized self-served portions, taste, subsidized buffet incentives or menu variety, rather than attendance forecasting. Rules handle recipe/batch/safety; predictive ML handles demand. Grounded Gemini is plausible only for proven consented unstructured last-minute event/menu changes before the last reversible cooking decision, with source links and chef approval. Incremental benefit over rules, incumbent tools or basic LLM = NOT TESTED. Strongest rejection: generic AI cannot prevent waste already left on diners' plates; cheap portion changes and incumbents may suffice.


FOOD-03N food-safety and falsification: Keep edible prep mistakes, untouched safely held surplus, buffet-exposed discard, edible plate returns, inedible matter and packaging separate. Never assume exposed buffet/plate food can be reused. Maintain food temperatures, allergen and veg/Jain segregation, adequate nutrition and choices, diner satisfaction and privacy. Proposed, NOT RUN: 28-day matched-weekday audit of two consenting Indian office kitchens. Record actual diner-meals, anonymous QR/POS headcounts, menus, procurement cutoff, batch/replenishment time, food temperatures, stockouts, cost and labor; independently tare-weigh each stage per ACTUAL meal served. Compare A current practice; B manual scales + half portions/smaller plates + staged cooking; C existing POS and rules/simple forecasts; D consented grounded Gemini exception queue with human chef approval. Reject GenAI if B/C eliminate actionable waste, relevant exceptions occur too late, D degrades quality/nutrition/safety, or data access fails. No partner, model run or savings measured. Problem Value /100 WITHHELD; separate technical 40/impact 25/innovation 25/UX 10 UNSCORED. DEFER generic office buffet GenAI, NARROW low-cost validation; no final winner. Next distinct investigation: office procurement cutoff and untouched surplus, not repeated plate-only estimates.


FOOD-03N non-JAPAC counterevidence: Orr and Goossens (16 Jan 2024) studied two German corporate canteens using seven non-AI measures, including smaller portions and plates. Canteen A recorded total waste 151 to 51 g/meal; plate 108 to 29 g and overproduction 42 to 22 g. Canteen B total 89 to 49 g/meal; plate 48 to 23 g and overproduction 40 to 26 g. https://doi.org/10.3390/su16020785


FOOD-03N caveat on German study: 742 kg (Nov 2022) and 399 kg (Apr 2023) are monthly snapshots; the 343 kg difference is not a cumulative six-month figure. Canteen A also changed meal format and closed Fridays, confounding attribution. Production-process waste excluded. No AI test. Article CC BY; raw meal records unavailable to this audit.


14 Oct 2026 23:35 IST | FOOD-03O | Japanese university cafeteria last-batch procurement and unsold prepared rice | Provisional DEFER generic GenAI; NARROW only after higher-residual site screening. Original 2017 Kyoto Prefectural University study: five weekdays of edible waste weighed 19–23 Oct 2015; ~500 cafeteria users/day. Source: https://doi.org/10.14912/jsmcwm.28.0_115 .
FOOD-03O PRIMARY MASS BALANCE (Takahashi, Saito & Yamakawa, 2017; five-day daily averages). The original full two-page proceedings paper is freely readable at https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jsmcwm/28/0/28_115/_pdf/-char/ja . Researchers weighed edible food only, removing inedible and nonfood material. Unsold prepared food: 7.321 kg/day; refrigerated rice for next-day service: 6.120 kg/day; staff purchases: 1.002 kg/day; these two routes redirected 7.122 kg/day (about 97% of unsold food), NOT prevention at production. Remaining unsold edible disposal: 0.199 kg/day. Edible plate returns: 1.338 kg/day. Final edible disposal: 1.537 kg/day (0.199 + 1.338). About 500 students/staff used the cafeteria daily, but exact meal denominators by observed day were not published. Dividing by this APPROXIMATE daily user count gives unsold 0.014642 kg/user, redirected 0.014244 kg/user, discarded unserved 0.000398 kg/user, plate 0.002676 kg/user, and final disposal 0.003074 kg/user; NONE is a validated actual-meal denominator. Authors rounded plate waste to 3 g/customer. The 84% unsold / 16% plate split applies BEFORE redirection, not to final disposal. Preparation errors and serving-line exposed waste were not separately measured. Salad-bar repurposing 0.668 kg/day may overlap other accounting and must not be added to redirection totals. The university had about 2,000 students; registered students are not the meal denominator. Study manager interviews Aug 2015-Jan 2016, source J-STAGE published 29 Nov 2017.
FOOD-03O additional original evidence: Japanese university reports show very low plate leftovers after simple portion choices. Source details pending.
Aino University original July 2024 report: 2023 plate leftovers 1.7 to 4.4 g per meal; other food refuse 0.7 to 1.9 g per meal, not verified edible. Reference: https://univ.aino.ac.jp/pickup/2024/07/1238.php


FOOD-03Q: Thai school lunch study measured 780 pupil lunch plates over five days in 2020. See Petchoo et al., 2022, DOI 10.1017/jns.2022.31.
FOOD-03Q evidence: The observed Thai school sample comprised 540 kindergarten and 240 primary lunches. Mean edible plate leftovers were 71.4 and 32 grams per sampled lunch respectively. Enrollment totals are not actual meal denominators.
Primary original study URL: https://doi.org/10.1017/jns.2022.31
FOOD-03Q independent corroboration: Zuhra et al. (1 April 2026) weighed leftovers for 106 Indonesian students at three East Aceh schools over a ten-day menu cycle. Mean plate waste was 24.3% of served food.
Indonesian comparison: Middle school 29.8%, high school 16.5%. Exact edible kg per actual meal and stage breakdown unavailable in inspected abstract. https://doi.org/10.56303/jhnresearch.v5i1.924
FOOD-03Q counterevidence: Tien et al. (8 Aug 2024) tested blanching and seasoning broccoli in Taiwan, then tracked primary-school vegetable leftovers. Observed aggregate waste was 6.5% of served vegetables; not a proven causal reduction.
FOOD-03Q low-cost alternatives: Meal headcounts, POS, manual scales, recipe cards, age-based ladles, smaller first rice portions with optional seconds, staff taste tests and basic attendance forecasts. Buyer willingness and small-site price: UNKNOWN.
FOOD-03Q AI hypothesis: Source-grounded, consented teacher feedback could be turned into cook-facing exception notes, subject to dietitian/teacher approval. Incremental advantage over rules, basic language models and existing tools NOT TESTED.
FOOD-03Q test NOT RUN: 28 school-day matched-menu audit in two consenting schools. Weigh edible preparation, untouched surplus, serving-line and plate leftovers separately per ACTUAL lunch; record procurement, attendance, portions and nutrient intake.
FOOD-03Q provisional NARROW. Problem Value /100 WITHHELD; technical judging 40/25/25/10 UNSCORED. No pilot, model evaluation, measured savings, verified Indian small-school market or final winner.
FOOD-03Q: Thai School Lunch was already used for ten-day menu planning and procurement at both study schools.
FOOD-03Q: Kindergarten rice servings were about twice the guideline; primary about 1.5 times.
FOOD-03Q: Meat, vegetables and fruits were frequently insufficient, making nutritional adequacy a key constraint.
FOOD-03Q Thai article corrigendum, 23 June 2023: https://doi.org/10.1017/jns.2023.56
FOOD-03Q Thai School Lunch official planner: https://www.thaischoollunch.in.th/
FOOD-03Q Thailand national agency report on planner, 2018: https://www.nstda.or.th/en/images/pdf/annualreport18.pdf
FOOD-03Q Thai article is CC BY 4.0. Raw attendance, procurement and per-pupil records were not verified available.
FOOD-03Q: Budget, emissions, water and avoidable kg savings remain UNKNOWN; observed plate waste is not all preventable.
FOOD-03Q test comparator: current practice vs manual scales/ladles vs rules/forecasts vs approved grounded AI.
FOOD-03Q: Enrollment-based schoolwide totals were extrapolated.


FOOD-03R | 15 Oct 2026 | Banquet late-course waste: research completed; append details pending.
FOOD-03R: Hong Kong Friends of the Earth 2010 report measured approximately 400 kg leftover across 104 banquet tables. Late courses had more leftovers. This is 3.85 kg per table, not per diner.
Source HK original annual report, 2010, page 17: https://ftp.foe.org.hk/FileUpload/AnnualReport/2010_annualreport.pdf . Actual diners, course-level kg, edible fractions, prep/line/plate split, procurement and savings remain UNKNOWN. Public PDF; dataset and reuse license unverified.
FOOD-03R Beijing corroboration: Cao et al., online 28 Nov 2020, observed 28 wedding-related banquets and 443 tables in 2015-2016. Fifteen ceremonial weddings averaged 239 diners and 19.08 dishes/table, 295.32 g waste per diner-meal (0.29532 kg), 25.35% food wasted and 70.58 kg per event. Thirteen thank-you banquets averaged 66.46 diners, 13.84 dishes/table, 144.27 g per diner-meal (0.14427 kg), 17.02% wasted and 9.59 kg per event. DIFFERENT menus, sizes and spend confound comparison; NOT a causal effect of dish count. No prep/line/plate split or independent scale protocol confirmed. Original: https://www.progressingeography.com/CN/abstract/article/1007-6301/48039 ; DOI: https://doi.org/10.18306/dlkxjz.2020.09.013 . Copyright reserved; raw data not verified accessible.
 reported groups: Chinese banquet 75.19 g starch + 8.06 g meat + 24.67 g fruit/veg = 107.92 g; dinner buffet 70.05 g; breakfast buffet 135.26 g; finger food 44.81 g. Kitchen and banquet bins mixed prep, line, plate and spoilage. Small n=4/style; event attendance, procurement, per-course masses and avoidability unverified. Their 96.28% dinner-buffet statistic is food's share of SOLID WASTE, not food waste as share of meals. Original full PDF: https://ph01.tci-thaijo.org/index.php/aer/article/download/257561/173953/994558 ; DOI https://doi.org/10.35762/AER.2024057 . Article CC BY-NC 4.0; raw dataset access/license UNKNOWN.
FOOD-03R host-approved smaller last batch. Distinct root cause may be ritual multi-course sequencing and late-service signals, rather than attendance error. A rule-based headcount/course-completion tally, smaller first batch, manual scale, cited exception proposals ONLY with explicit host/chef approval; incremental value over a structured checkbox, basic LLM, rules and ML NOT TESTED.
FOOD-03R Winnow forecasts using occupancy and historical waste: https://www.winnowsolutions.com/winnow-foresight . NEW Indian Neviscater advertises guest-count recipe sizing, procurement and event waste tracking; published Standard ₹24,000 independent proof of real deployment or affordable small-kitchen buyers; buyer willingness and viable segment UNKNOWN.
FOOD-03R critical constraints: contractual menu/guest service, food temperature, allergen and Jain/vegetarian segregation, guest satisfaction, staff workload and nutrition. Weigh edible prep mistakes, untouched safe kitchen surplus, exposed serving-line/shared platter, individual plate returns, and inedible matter SEPARATELY, with actual diner-meals as denominator. FSSAI 2019 surplus rules permit safe unused food NOT previously served, with records, labeling and safe handling: https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Gazette_Notification_Surplus_Food_06_08_2019.pdf . Do not treat plate or exposed platter waste as donation-eligible. Observed kg are NOT verified preventable kg; Indian savings remain UNKNOWN.
FOOD-03R CLARIFICATION: Some earlier notes were interrupted while saving. The complete independent Thai source is Srijuntrapun & Sukwong, published 27 Dec 2024, four physically sampled events per catering style in Bangkok-area hotels.
Thai Table 1 nominal edible-category waste per meal: Chinese banquet 75.19 g starch + 8.06 g meat + 24.67 g produce = 107.92 g; dinner buffet 70.05 g; breakfast buffet 135.26 g; finger-food 44.81 g.
Thai study: kitchen and banquet bins were combined. Preparation, serving-line and plate waste were not separated. Actual guest counts and event-level procurement were not available.


FOOD-03R final verdict: NARROW. No model run, measured saving, partner or small-kitchen willingness-to-pay verified.
Strongest rejection: paid banquet courses and prestige require abundance; most leftover dishes may already have reached tables.
Cheaper alternatives: smaller final batch, headcount tally, captain-to-chef checkbox, POS, manual weighing, menu simplification, and ordinary forecasts.
AI hypothesis: consented captain notes summarized with sources for chef approval; advantage over rules, ML or a basic LLM is untested.
Falsification NOT RUN: audit 20 consented Indian events, logging actual diner-meals, course timing, procurement cutoff, signed menus, temperatures and independent edible kg at each stage.
Compare current practice with approved captain checkbox and batch rules, then replay messages against basic LLM, ML and grounded Gemini with human approval.
Reject AI if rules suffice, messages arrive after cooking, safety/quality/stockouts worsen or net labor cost rises. Problem Value /100 WITHHELD; technical 40/25/25/10 UNSCORED.
Competitor links: https://info.leanpath.com/snap-ai ; https://www.winnowsolutions.com/winnow-foresight
FSSAI 2019 restricts surplus donations to safe unused portions not served. Temperature, allergy, veg/Jain and host contract rules take priority.
FOOD-03R Thai data are independent field measurements, but their pooled bins cannot establish separately avoidable edible kilograms for last-course release.


FOOD-03S | 15 Oct 2026 | Thai hotel buffet breakfast plate-waste research. Details pending.
FOOD-03S evidence 1: Somsuk, Udomwitid and Sompornserm (30 September 2026) report a quasi-experimental Thai hotel breakfast buffet study of 850 convenience-sampled diners with digital plate weighing. Relative to standard service, loss-framed signs were associated with 37.49 g less plate waste per diner, gain-framed signs with 34.02 g less, and information-default signs with 19.50 g less (reported p<0.01). These are treatment-control differences, NOT absolute edible kg/meal, verified savings or GenAI results. Source: https://so06.tci-thaijo.org/index.php/JSSP/article/view/297626 .
FOOD-03S evidence caveat: The Thai paper's abstract does not report per-arm n, absolute baseline waste, edible/in-edible sorting, allocation by service day, procurement, menu, occupancy, buffet-line mass, pre-service mass or cost. The full PDF could not be accessed in this audit; raw diner data and data-reuse rights UNKNOWN. Journal displays CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Confidence moderate for reported group differences, low for causal or Indian-site transfer. The 850 is TOTAL study diners, not treatment-arm denominator. Never multiply a reported group difference by 850 and call it measured avoided food.
FOOD-03S independent non-AI operations evidence: Hasna et al., published 24 May 2026, qualitative Sheraton Grand Jakarta hotel buffet case: occupancy-based plans, staged batch cooking, smaller buffet containers, gradual refill, waste logs and food-safety-constrained surplus handling were already used. No measured reduction or verified zero disposal reported. https://ejournal.uin-suska.ac.id/index.php/jti/article/view/39625 . CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Wu and Teng, Taiwan two-buffet-chain study (28 Dec 2022), 15 manager/chef/staff interviews, found menu design, forecasting, supplier and service redesign and tracking strategies; not a controlled savings trial. https://doi.org/10.3390/foods12010162 . CC BY 4.0.
FOOD-03S stage ledger: Thai intervention reports only a plate-waste DIFFERENCE 0.01950–0.03749 kg/diner vs control, not absolute baseline and not confirmed edible. Absolute edible plate kg/actual meal UNKNOWN. Edible prep kg/actual meal UNKNOWN; untouched safe unserved kg/actual meal UNKNOWN; exposed buffet-line kg/actual meal UNKNOWN; inedible and wet mass UNKNOWN. Taiwan 2016 mixed kg/meal cannot be combined with Thai plate differences. Actual menu, attendance, purchases, costs and food temperatures unreported in accessible sources. Verified preventable edible kg, Indian budget, water and emissions outcomes all UNKNOWN.
FOOD-03S incumbent challenge: Winnow Foresight now offers standalone mobile item-level hotel breakfast forecasts from occupancy and prior waste, with photo-based leftover estimates; public hotel savings are VENDOR claims, not independently controlled comparisons. https://www.winnowsolutions.com/winnow-foresight . Leanpath offers scale-based trackers, portable Tracker Lite and event/buffet photo logging. https://www.leanpath.com/products/food-waste-tracking/ . Lightspeed POS already handles ingredient inventory, recipe costing and wastage records. https://www.lightspeedhq.com/pos/restaurant/inventory/ . Prices, willingness to pay and viable affordable Indian small-kitchen segment UNKNOWN.
FOOD-03S substitutes and rejection: Cheapest baseline is translated loss-framed signage, smaller initial servings with optional seconds, measured plate/buffet bins, actual booking headcounts, staged refill and Excel/POS forecasting. Strongest rejection: guest overloading is behavioral, signs already show a measured association, and existing hotel forecasting tools address production. A Gemini agent might ground consented multilingual staff exceptions into chef-approved instructions, but rules, predictive ML and an ordinary LLM already handle most steps; incremental Gemini effect NOT TESTED. Never autonomously modify food safety, allergens, veg/Jain segregation or nutritional choice; never reuse plate returns or exposed buffet food.
FOOD-03S falsification PROPOSED, NOT RUN: 28 matched breakfast service days in two consenting small Indian buffets, with independent tare weighing of edible prep mistakes, untouched safe kitchen surplus, exposed buffet line, edible plate returns, and wet/inedible matter. Denominator = ACTUAL diners verified with POS/bookings. Compare A status quo; B standardized loss-framed signs + smaller optional first servings + manual scales; C B plus headcount-based staged cooking and simple demand forecasts; D C plus grounded Gemini exception routing with chef approval. Record menus, purchase cutoff, food temperatures, nutrition/choice, guest satisfaction, stockouts, staff minutes and net food cost. Reject AI if B/C capture the improvement, D adds no material benefit net of costs, or safety/quality worsens. No partner, model run, physical saving or impact factor verified. DEFER generic AI buffet nudges; NARROW only to proven unstructured exceptions. Problem Value /100 WITHHELD; judging 40/25/25/10 UNSCORED; no final winner.
FOOD-03S Taiwan 2016 independent buffet audit: original source link pending.
The Taiwanese audit estimated mixed waste of 450 to 929 grams per diner; the figure includes material beyond edible plate leftovers.
FOOD-03S stronger Taiwan original PDF review: Lin's 2016 field study collected 14 days of site data per restaurant during Apr–Jun 2012, recording actual diners by meal period. Average customers/day: hotel A 677, B 812, C 519. Table 7 separates buffet COUNTER waste from GUEST plate/beverage returns: A 92.66 g and 132.88 g per diner-meal; B 72.51 g and 183.64 g; C 140.40 g and 307.37 g. These are physically measured wet streams with beverages and inedible status unverified; NOT verified edible kilograms. Preparation edible waste was NOT separately measured.
FOOD-03S Taiwan breakfast-specific Table 7 wet masses per ACTUAL breakfast diner: hotel A buffet counter 51.15 g, guest returns 84.62 g; hotel B 108.05 g counter, 111.11 g guest; hotel C 78.06 g counter, 222.97 g guest. These are NOT edible-only, and not preparation waste. Across all meal periods, dining-area buffet-counter waste is lower in the open-kitchen hotel B, but kitchen visibility and diner turnover are confounded; no causal proof. This reinforces a low-tech option: staff visually monitor trays and refill gradually.

structuredContent.content:
﻿LANE 2 — INSTITUTIONAL KITCHENS
Start 14 Oct 2026 | India metro institutions first | Ownership: This document only
Mission: identify high-severity avoidable food waste in schools, colleges, hostels, offices, canteens, caterers, hospitals and elder-care facilities, disaggregating preparation loss, buffet leftovers and plate waste. Read Research Control Room per run.


HYPOTHESIS FOOD-03
Actual portions prepared fail to match attendance, demand, diet and timing; consequences = kilograms food discarded per meal, operating costs, wasted water/energy/land and possibly budgets available for food. Never count nutrition restriction or safe food handling as "waste" without context. Students and patients are protected populations; food suitability, allergies and sanitation constrain decisions.


COMPETITION
Winnow and Leanpath already provide AI vision logging, restaurant/kitchen waste categorization, dashboards and behavioral coaching; ordinary headcounts, procurement spreadsheets, Excel, ERP, menu planning and kitchen staff judgments are cheap substitutes. Do not claim image-recognition novel. Study small-facility adoption, economics and locally verified friction.


RESEARCH QUEUE
1. Find JAPAC ORIGINAL weighed food waste per meal for one institution type, with numerator, denominator, pre/post measurement.
2. Identify original causes (menu preference, class attendance, buffet uncertainty, hospital diet, serving-size design) and which are actually actionable.
3. Check adoption and product capability for Winnow/Leanpath, and local low-cost providers, in 2026; analyze affordability only with sourced quotes or documented budgets.
4. Seek legally/publicly available meal count + waste datasets, and external validity of any intervention studies.
5. Compare Gemini explanation/workflow automation and human-safe orchestration vs simple forecast / deterministic count. Distinguish pre-service leftovers from served food, donation eligibility.
6. Kill if straightforward count-based forecasting or existing product adequate, or no authentic data/authority to change prep.


CURRENT VERDICT: ADVANCE TO DATA ACCESS AUDIT; residual unmet need UNKNOWN; experiment NOT RUN.
SOURCE STARTERS
https://www.winnowsolutions.com/
https://www.leanpath.com/
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S095965262403645X
https://wedocs.unep.org/handle/20.500.11822/45230
APPEND DATED RUN ENTRIES BELOW.


Research update: original institutional kitchen studies located on 14 October 2026.


FOOD-03A | Campus mess attendance and preparation | 14 Oct 2026
Provisional verdict: NARROW. Investigate a specific gap in knowing how many students will actually eat a particular meal; do not presume GenAI is necessary.


India original physical baseline: Davison et al. (published 3 May 2022) measured approximately 45 kg of daily food waste at a Maharashtra university canteen serving 375 students (120 g per catered student-day) during Jan–Feb 2020. Following reopening, about 9 kg/day was measured among 150 students (60 g/student-day) in Dec 2020–Jan 2021. The apparent 50% per-person decline cannot be assigned to one intervention because occupancy, dining format, menus, and outside eating options changed during COVID. These are daily figures, not per meal, and do not separate preparation, service, and plate waste. Underlying records are not publicly shared. Source: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14095486


Independent India qualitative study: Rajalakshmi and Harshavardhini (April 2025), interviews with 50 hostel students, identified outside ordering without notice (20% of respondents), overpreparation (45%) and poor taste (60%) among perceived causes. These percentages are not weighed waste incidence. Source: https://doi.org/10.4103/jme.jme_118_24


Japan independently weighed evidence: Nakagiri et al. (PLOS ONE, 26 Feb 2024) measured returned side-dish containers at 20 elementary/junior-high schools supplied by one communal kitchen across 116 days. The median leftover rate was 20.1% for 250 selected high-leftover side dishes (range 0–96.9%), not the average for all meals or all food. Class size, nutrition-teacher assignment and elapsed time since cooking were associated with leftovers; adjusted R-squared 0.236. Supporting XLSX tables are published and could support reproducible analysis, though transferability to India is unknown. Source: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0298691


Additional India evidence: Reshmi and Srikanth (24 June 2025) observed/interviewed 11 Bengaluru educational cafeterias, identifying weak first-in-first-out inventory, expiration/freshness issues, forecasting and cold storage. No verified edible kilograms per meal or controlled intervention. These inventory failures differ from attendance-driven waste. Source: https://doi.org/10.36713/epra22674


Critical competitive correction: Winnow Foresight currently advertises standalone, mobile-only item-level production forecasts based on occupancy and waste history, without additional hardware. Leanpath offers tablet-only Tracker Lite, mobile Snap AI, and plate-waste analysis. Therefore no-hardware forecasting and AI plate logging are not unique. Published Indian small-site adoption, pricing and independent performance remain unknown. Sources: https://www.winnowsolutions.com/winnow-foresight and https://www.leanpath.com/products/


Root cause and alternatives: The Indian canteen study describes unpredictable mess attendance, students choosing outside meals, regional menu preferences and self-service overfilling. During COVID, better student attendance information, table service, fewer outside choices and smaller servings all changed together. Cheap alternatives are opt-out deadlines, basic headcount plus day-of-week forecasting, historical portions, smaller initial servings with seconds, manual waste weighing, and menu feedback. No evidence yet shows these fail. Food quality and sufficient meals must be maintained.


AI-specific hypothesis only: If dining intentions arrive as messy, inconsistent notes, a grounded Gemini workflow might classify changes and request confirmation, while deterministic code computes quantities. But standard forms, simple rules and conventional forecasting may be more reliable and cheaper. No model evaluation, consented campus integration, procurement integration or product deployment has been performed.


Falsification test (NOT RUN): Obtain permission for 14–28 days of actual diners by meal, timestamped advance dining intentions, dish-level planned versus cooked quantities, and separately weighed edible unserved food, plate waste and inedible preparation scraps. Compare current chef planning, simple headcount/opt-out rules, conventional forecasting, and an optional Gemini-assisted interpretation workflow on held-out days. Outcomes: kilograms of avoidable edible waste per actual meal served, forecasting error, food sufficiency, meal satisfaction, operator time and ingredient cost. Use food-specific environmental factors only with a defensible avoided-production/disposal counterfactual. Stop if rules work as well, existing competitors already solve the workflow, or authentic data is inaccessible.


Research status: underlying severity evidenced at selected sites; prevalence, edible fraction, unmet need after alternatives, willingness to pay and technical advantage UNKNOWN. Problem Value Score /100 withheld. Hackathon rubric technical 40%, impact 25%, innovation 25%, UX 10% remains separate. Strongest rejection: current attendance rules or Winnow/Leanpath eliminate the incremental AI value. Do not claim avoided emissions, hunger reduction or savings. NEXT: data-access audit of one India campus operator and public Japanese supplementary XLSX reproduction.




RESEARCH UPDATE — 14 OCT 2026, 10:31 IST — FOOD-03B: HOSPITAL WARD↔KITCHEN MEAL-STATUS HANDOFF
Research stage: independently corroborated severity + root-cause evidence → incumbent red-team → data-access falsification. Distinct from previous campus-mess FOOD-03A. VERDICT: NARROW TO HOSPITAL MEAL-STATUS EXCEPTIONS; DO NOT ASSUME GENAI VALUE.


PRECISE WORKFLOW AND USERS
A hospital dietitian prescribes the permitted diet; ward nurse and bed-management team record admissions, transfers, discharge, nil-by-mouth/procedure status and meal requests; kitchen manager commits production quantities before a cutoff; staff plate and deliver trays; patient may eat, defer or decline. Meal demand becomes inaccurate when clinically authorized status changes do not reach the kitchen before irreversible preparation. This is a candidate exception-handling problem, not a proposal to override clinical diets or automatically suppress nutrition.


NEW ORIGINAL JAPAC QUANTIFICATION — AUSTRALIA
E-L2-2026-01: Ni et al., Waste Management, published 15 Jan 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.wasman.2025.115242. Audit performed Sep–Oct 2023 at ONE 355-bed acute-care hospital in Adelaide; kitchen also supplied eight external sites (393 beds), so its total kitchen denominator is not identical to the three wards used for plate observations. Direct weighing + photographic/visual estimates across a full menu cycle: seven breakfasts, 21 lunches, 21 dinners; 2,616 plated meals from selected wards, 2,214 plates returned and audited (402, or 15%, missing). Mean kitchen food waste = 134.1 kg/day or 170.4 g per meal PRODUCED. Breakdown: unserved 117.5 kg/day = 149.3 g/meal (87.6% of kitchen food waste), preparation 16.3 kg/day = 20.7 g/meal, spoilage 0.3 kg/day = 0.4 g/meal. Edible preparation fraction = 14.7 kg/day = 18.7 g/meal; inedible = 1.5 kg/day = 2.0 g/meal. Plate waste on the three observed wards averaged 0.7 kg per patient-DAY (NOT per meal), or 40.7% of food served; special diets 49.4% vs regular diets 36.4% in diet-identified subset, with pureed diets especially high. Article explicitly notes meals prepared for patients scheduled for surgery or discharge as one contributor to unserved food, but does NOT quantify its attributable fraction. Other limitations: single site; liquid waste excluded; 15% of plate trays not returned; hospital supplied offsite locations; prep work outsourced upstream in part; original individual-level dataset NOT shareable because authors lacked permission. No controlled AI intervention or avoidable share proven. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wasman.2025.115242

Previously documented Winnow Foresight (mobile-only production forecast) and Leanpath (plate/waste logging) remain relevant for measurement and forecasts but are not replacements for clinical diet order controls.
Cheaper controls: existing HIMS/EMR ADT event feed + rules for meal cutoff, NPO/fasting flags from authorized clinical orders, ward-to-kitchen confirmation, census-based production buffers, late change exceptions, patient opt-in where clinically appropriate, audit trail and manual scale. None requires GenAI to perform core logic. Need evidence these controls fail in an accessible target institution before advancing.


POTENTIAL AI ROLE — HYPOTHESIS, NOT DEMONSTRATED
A constrained, grounded Gemini/agent workflow might reconcile unstructured ward messages, late procedure notices, dietitian-approved menu constraints and kitchen exceptions, classify ambiguous statuses, request human confirmation and create traceable alerts to a deterministic scheduling system. It must NEVER infer or alter diet orders, NPO status, allergies or medical restrictions from generated text. Authenticated EHR/HIMS event feeds and rules take precedence; model must not handle identifiable clinical records without approvals, and no automated cancellation of clinically required meals. General LLM plus rules and established HIMS integration are strong comparators; agent complexity may add latency and safety risk. The presence of messy text does not establish incremental AI benefit.


MEASUREMENT / IMPACT BOUNDARIES
Primary numerator: grams/kg of avoidable EDIBLE unserved food discarded before any patient handling, by dish and meal service. Denominator: meals actually produced, and optionally kg per patient-meal ordered/served. Track plate waste separately (g/plate and % of served), and prep edible vs inedible separately. Measure meal-order change-to-kitchen latency, duplicate trays, late changes, number of clinically required meals fulfilled on time, patient nutrient adequacy, kitchen labor and ingredient cost. Do not multiply Australia's 149.3 g/meal by Indian hospital census and claim a prediction. Do not infer all unserved food is avoidable; safety buffers and diet requirements matter. Any CO2e/water estimate needs food-specific composition, local supply chain and avoided-production/disposal counterfactual; AI inference and extra computing footprint must be deducted where material. Social benefit = protecting patient meal access/nutrition and hospital budgets, NOT a claim of donations or reduced malnutrition.

Published aggregate figures are available under open-access journal license; original hospital event and meal records NOT available to this project. ONE DECISIVE FALSIFICATION TEST — NOT RUN
With authorized hospital and clinical oversight, retrospectively obtain 14–28 days of pseudonymized time-stamped (a) meal orders and actual plating cutoff, (b) clinically approved diet/order status, (c) admission/discharge/transfer/procedure event timestamps, (d) kitchen production and weighed edible unserved/plate waste, (e) meals delivered and missed or delayed. Establish exact number and kg of trays prepared AFTER an authoritative status change that a basic ADT/HIMS rule could have prevented. On held-out periods compare: A current process, B deterministic event-driven ADT sync + cutoff/confirmation rules, C existing meal-management vendor or feature, D optional Gemini interpreting only residual unstructured approved notes. Success requires an independently observed, recurring residual kg of avoidable edible waste and no clinically missed nutrition; Gemini must demonstrably improve precision/recall, human minutes or resolution time beyond B/C, without safety errors. REJECT GenAI angle if B/C eliminate most avoidable waste, or if clinical data access impossible. A public synthetic scenario can demonstrate technical handling but cannot pass the impact gate.
